- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often underestimates — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if recent 10-day average is > forecast, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often lags behind true price movement — increase forecast sensitivity to recent 5-day sentiment shifts.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.33), model tends to underestimate — apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- If true price drops sharply after model peak, model often fails to adjust — add “lag correction” rule: if forecast > true price by >3%, reduce next forecast by 0.75–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
